# Research report

King of Norway Magnus Barefoot launched aggressive military campaigns in this region that was at times independent of external control and was known to the Norse as what?

## Answer

Suðreyjar (Southern Isles) [E9] [E10] [E11] [E12] [E3]

## Findings (not verified)

- Magnus Barefoot's expedition into the Irish Sea sought to assert Norwegian rule over the Kingdom of the Isles. [E3]
- The Kingdom of the Isles comprised the Hebrides, the islands of the Firth of Clyde and the Isle of Man from the 9th to the 13th centuries AD. [E7] [E8]
- At times the rulers of the Kingdom of the Isles were independent of external control. [E11] [E12]
- The islands were known to the Norse as the "Suðreyjar", or "Southern Isles". [E9] [E10]

## Unresolved questions

None identified by the system. Checker decisions remain subject to human audit.

## Evidence

### [E1] Magnus Barefoot
{"sentence_ids": [0], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 264}

> Magnus Olafsson (Old Norse: "Magnús Óláfsson", Norwegian: "Magnus Olavsson"; 1073 – 24 August 1103), better known as Magnus Barefoot (Old Norse: "Magnús berfœttr", Norwegian: "Magnus Berrføtt"), was King of Norway (as Magnus III) from 1093 until his death in 1103.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnus_Barefoot
### [E2] King Magnus' Halt railway station
{"sentence_ids": [1], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 72}

>  It takes its name from the nearby grave of Viking King Magnus Barefoot.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Magnus%27_Halt_railway_station
### [E3] Battle of Anglesey Sound
{"sentence_ids": [1], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 275}

>  The battle was fought between Magnus Barefoot, King of Norway, and the Anglo-Norman earls Hugh of Montgomery and Hugh d'Avranches, and took place as part of Magnus Barefoot's expedition into the Irish Sea, which sought to assert Norwegian rule over the Kingdom of the Isles.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Anglesey_Sound
### [E4] Battle of Stamford Bridge
{"sentence_ids": [3], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 303}

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Stamford_Bridge

# Research report

King of Norway Magnus Barefoot launched aggressive military campaigns in this region that was at times independent of external control and was known to the Norse as what?

## Answer

Suðreyjar [E7] [E5]

## Supported findings

- Magnus Barefoot's reign was marked by aggressive military campaigns and conquest, particularly in the Norse-dominated parts of the British Isles and Ireland, extending his rule to the Kingdom of the Isles and Dublin. [E5]
- The Kingdom of the Isles comprised the Hebrides, the islands of the Firth of Clyde and the Isle of Man from the 9th to the 13th centuries AD. [E11]
- The islands were known to the Norse as the "Suðreyjar", or "Southern Isles", as distinct from the "Norðreyjar" or Northern Isles of Orkney and Shetland. [E7] [E8]
- At times the rulers of the Kingdom of the Isles were independent of external control, although for much of the period they had overlords in Norway, Ireland, England, Scotland or Orkney. [E9] [E10]

## Unresolved questions

None identified by the system. Checker decisions remain subject to human audit.

## Answer

Insufficient verified evidence to answer.

- Magnus Barefoot's reign was marked by aggressive military campaigns and conquest, particularly in the Norse-dominated parts of the British Isles and Ireland, where he extended his rule to the Kingdom of the Isles and Dublin. [E5]
- The Kingdom of the Isles comprised the Hebrides, the islands of the Firth of Clyde and the Isle of Man from the 9th to the 13th centuries AD. [E7] [E8]

What was the name of the bear promoted to corporal in the Polish army, and celebrated by an ongoing fundraising trust based in Scotland?

## Answer

Wojtek [E1] [E2] [E3]

## Supported findings

- Wojtek was a Syrian brown bear purchased as a cub in Hamadan, Iran, by Polish II Corps soldiers. [E3]
- Wojtek was enlisted officially as a soldier with the rank of private and subsequently promoted to corporal. [E1]
- The Wojtek Memorial Trust is a Scottish Charity (SCO41057) established in 2009 to celebrate the life of Wojtek, "the Soldier Bear". [E2]
- The Trust also aims to promote wider understanding of historic and current links between the peoples of Poland and Scotland. [E4]

## Unresolved questions

None identified by the system. Checker decisions remain subject to human audit.

## Evidence

- John Dufresne is an American author of French Canadian descent born in Worcester, Massachusetts. [E7]

# Research report

Which British first-generation jet-powered medium bomber was used in the South West Pacific theatre of World War II?

## Answer

English Electric Canberra [E1] [E2]

## Findings (not verified)

- The English Electric Canberra is a British first-generation jet-powered medium bomber manufactured during the 1950s. [E1]
- No. 2 Squadron RAAF saw action as a bomber unit in the South West Pacific theatre of World War II and was equipped with English Electric Canberra jets. [E2]
- The Canberra became the RAF's first jet-powered bomber aircraft when introduced in May 1951. [E5]

## Unresolved questions

- The evidence does not explicitly state that the Canberra itself flew in the South West Pacific theatre during World War II; E2 links the squadron to that theatre and separately to Canberra jets, so the direct wartime use of the Canberra there is not confirmed.

## Evidence

# Research report

Which British first-generation jet-powered medium bomber was used in the South West Pacific theatre of World War II?

## Answer

Insufficient verified evidence to answer.

## Supported findings

- The English Electric Canberra is a British first-generation jet-powered medium bomber manufactured during the 1950s. [E1]

## Unresolved questions

- The evidence does not explicitly state that the Canberra itself was used in the South West Pacific theatre during World War II; E3 links the squadron's WWII service and its later Canberra equipment in the same sentence, and the Canberra entered RAF service in May 1951 (E4), after WWII.
- The British first-generation jet-powered medium bomber used in the South West Pacific theatre of World War II was the English Electric Canberra. — E1 confirms the Canberra is a British first-generation jet-powered medium bomber, and E3 mentions a bomber unit seeing action in the South West Pacific theatre and being equipped with Canberra jets, but E3 does not state the Canberra itself was used in the South West Pacific theatre during WWII; the two facts are only juxtaposed, not linked.
- No. 2 Squadron RAAF saw action as a bomber unit in the South West Pacific theatre of World War II and was equipped with English Electric Canberra jets. — Numerical literals not found in cited passages: 2

## Evidence

### [E1] English Electric Canberra

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tupolev_Tu-12
### [E3] No. 2 Squadron RAAF
{"sentence_ids": [5], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 178}

>  It saw action as a bomber unit in the South West Pacific theatre of World War II and, equipped with English Electric Canberra jets, in the Malayan Emergency and the Vietnam War.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._2_Squadron_RAAF
### [E4] English Electric Canberra
{"sentence_ids": [4], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 175}

>  When the Canberra was introduced to service with the Royal Air Force (RAF), the type's first operator, in May 1951, it became the service's first jet-powered bomber aircraft.

# Research report

Which school is named after a person, Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology or Manhattan College? 

## Answer

Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology [E1]

## Findings (not verified)

- Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology is honored in the name of 19th-century Muslim reformer and philosopher Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, a person. [E1]
- Manhattan College is a private Roman Catholic liberal arts college located in the Bronx, New York City, and its name refers to the place Manhattan rather than a person. [E8] [E10]

## Unresolved questions

- No evidence explicitly states that Manhattan College is named after the place Manhattan; this is inferred from its location history (E10) and absence of any person named Manhattan in the evidence.

## Evidence

### [E1] Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology
{"sentence_ids": [1], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 116}

>  The university is honored in the name of notable 19th-century Muslim reformer and philosopher, Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Syed_University_of_Engineering_and_Technology
### [E2] Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology
{"sentence_ids": [0], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 156}

> Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology (known as "SSUET") is a private research university located in the urban area of Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Syed_University_of_Engineering_and_Technology
### [E3] Sir Syed College
{"sentence_ids": [0], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 62}

> Sir Syed College are colleges named after Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Syed_College
### [E4] Syed Mir Hassan
{"sentence_ids": [4], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 58}

>  Both brothers were great admirers of Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syed_Mir_Hassan
### [E5] Syed Mahmood
{"sentence_ids": [2], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 189}

>  Syed Mahmood also had a major role in assisting his father, Sir Syed Ahmed Khan in establishing the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, which later developed into Aligarh Muslim University.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syed_Mahmood
### [E6] Sir Syed Masjid

# Research report

Which school is named after a person, Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology or Manhattan College? 

## Answer

Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology [E1]

## Supported findings

- Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology is honored in the name of notable 19th-century Muslim reformer and philosopher Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. [E1]
- Manhattan College is a private, independent, Roman Catholic, liberal arts college located in the Bronx, New York City, United States. [E7]
- Manhattan College was originally established in 1853 by the Brothers of the Christian Schools as an academy for day students. [E11]

## Unresolved questions

- No supplied evidence states that Manhattan College is named after a person; the evidence describes its founding and location but not a personal namesake.

## Evidence

>  Syed Mahmood also had a major role in assisting his father, Sir Syed Ahmed Khan in establishing the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, which later developed into Aligarh Muslim University.

# Research report

Who was Chamberlain and Colonel of the military staff of The Merrie Monarch?

## Answer

Charles Hastings Judd [E1] [E3]

## Findings (not verified)

- Charles Hastings Judd served as Chamberlain and Colonel of the military staff of King Kalākaua and traveled with the monarch on his 1881 world tour. [E1]
- Kalākaua was sometimes called The Merrie Monarch and was the last king of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi. [E3]

## Unresolved questions

None identified by the system. Checker decisions remain subject to human audit.

## Evidence

### [E1] Charles Hastings Judd

{"sentence_ids": [1], "start_char": 0, "end_char": 200}

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kal%C4%81kaua

# Research report

Which former Republican won the presidential nomination at the 2012 United States Libertarian National Convention? 

## Answer

Gary Johnson [E1] [E9]

## Supported findings

- On May 5, 2012, Johnson received the most votes at the convention and became the official 2012 Libertarian presidential nominee. [E9]
- On December 28, 2011, Johnson withdrew his candidacy for the Republican nomination and declared his candidacy for the Libertarian Party's 2012 presidential nomination. [E3]
- Johnson had earlier declared his candidacy for the 2012 Republican Party presidential nomination. [E4]

## Unresolved questions

- Former Governor of New Mexico Gary Johnson won the presidential nomination at the 2012 Libertarian National Convention on the first ballot. — Numerical literals not found in cited passages: 2012

# Research report

Who wrote lyrics for both "Little Shop of Horrors" and the song "Be Our Guest?" 

## Answer

Howard Ashman [E1] [E7]

## Supported findings

- Howard Ashman wrote both the book and lyrics for the musical "Little Shop of Horrors" (1982). [E1]
- "Be Our Guest" is a song written by lyricist Howard Ashman and composer Alan Menken for Disney's "Beauty and the Beast" (1991). [E7]
- Ashman collaborated with Alan Menken on several works, writing lyrics while Menken composed the music. [E5]

## Unresolved questions

None identified by the system. Checker decisions remain subject to human audit.

## Evidence

### [E1] Howard Ashman

>  It is a film adaptation of the off-Broadway musical comedy of the same name by composer Alan Menken and writer Howard Ashman about a nerdy florist shop worker who finds out his venus fly trap can speak.

# Research report

Who wrote lyrics for both "Little Shop of Horrors" and the song "Be Our Guest?" 

## Answer

Howard Ashman [E1] [E7]

## Supported findings

- Howard Ashman wrote both the book and lyrics for the musical "Little Shop of Horrors" (1982). [E1]
- "Be Our Guest" is a song written by lyricist Howard Ashman and composer Alan Menken for Disney's "Beauty and the Beast" (1991). [E7]
- Ashman collaborated with Alan Menken on several works, writing lyrics while Menken composed the music. [E5]

## Unresolved questions

None identified by the system. Checker decisions remain subject to human audit.
